title: Count Number of Bad Pairs
summary: Given an array of integers, count the number of index pairs (i, j) where i is less than j and the difference between j and i does not match the difference between the values at j and i.
statement: Given an array of integers, count the number of index pairs (i, j) where i is less than j and the difference between j and i does not match the difference between the values at j and i.
constraints: For indexes i<j, a pair is good when j-i equals nums[j]-nums[i].
A bad pair is any index pair that is not good.
Return the number of bad unordered index pairs.
hints: Rearrange the good condition to nums[i]-i == nums[j]-j.
Count earlier occurrences of each value-index key while scanning.
Subtract the accumulated good-pair count from n(n-1)/2 total pairs.
Equal keys characterize exactly the good pairs, and every earlier equal key forms one such pair with the current index.
editorial: Equal keys characterize exactly the good pairs, and every earlier equal key forms one such pair with the current index.

tests.explanation: There is one good pair and five of the six total pairs are bad.
Every pair is good because value-index is constant, so the result is zero.
